The candidate defines exactly one predicate per declared proposition (key_found, has_matching_key, target_door_open, target_picked_up) with matching names, each taking exactly `env`, and correctly omits target_room_entered, which the machine does not use and which is not under Declared propositions. key_found implements the latch-reading semantics faithfully: it ORs the previous valuation (guarded for truthiness, accessed by subscript without `.get`) with the documented 7x7 view scan `cell[0] == 5`, so occluded keys behind walls or closed doors do not count and the latch persists once true; it can also be true on the first step when the key is visible at reset, as the reading allows. has_matching_key and target_door_open locate the locked door by place, not by `is_locked`: they derive the ball's room row via `y // (env.room_size - 1)` from a full-grid ball scan (guarded with `bc is not None`, with a safe default), scan the left-wall column `env.width - env.room_size` across the room block, and guard each cell with `door is not None and door.type == 'door'` before reading `color`/`is_open`, giving 'carries a key of the locked door's color' and 'locked door currently open (false again if shut)'. target_picked_up requires carrying a ball whose color matches the mission string built from `env.mission`, so only the designated object counts. All bodies are single expression returns using only allowed builtins (any, max, range) plus documented API attributes (env.grid.get, env.gen_obs()['image'], env.carrying, env.agent_pos, env.width/height, env.room_size, env.mission, door.is_open); no mutation, no invented attributes, no sibling calls, and no recursive history beyond the documented previous-valuation latch.
